dod_intent_evidence: US Navy contract for the V2.5 aircraft plus a $37M USAF/AFWERX award (June 2025) to 'rapidly scale' V3 into fielded production, confirmed by their own newsroom, Businesswire, and Austin Business Journal, and their own SBIR Phase II abstract.
score_evidence: "We are building the largest unmanned aircraft fleet in the world" / "impressive flight envelope" spec-bragging with zero comms/software architecture framing -> lab_language_intensity
no mention anywhere of DDIL/ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR/STIG despite scaling to a $37M USAF production contract -> deployment_awareness_absence
no mention of who operates, trains on, or maintains the aircraft in the field beyond generic "customer feedback" -> operator_absence

open roles include Senior Flight Test Engineer and Senior Subsystem Test Engineer (field/integration-adjacent for a hardware firm) alongside pure R&D roles -> hiring_profile_skew (partial credit, not maximal)
$37M AFWERX award explicitly to 'rapidly scale' V3, which is 'currently in testing' and targeted for 2026 readiness -> stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: The aircraft is marketed as 'fully autonomous, long-range' with no discussion of how command-and-control, mission updates, or telemetry survive the same remote, high-risk environments the airframe is built to physically endure.
blind_spots.operator_reality: An autonomous cargo drone flying to a denied or contested offshore platform or forward site needs a C2/telemetry link architecture that assumes intermittent or denied comms, the same failure class as the 30fps crowd-detection case; nothing on the site addresses what the aircraft does when it loses its link mid-mission.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Messaging is entirely airframe-performance focused (range, payload, endurance specs); the software/comms stack that makes 'fully autonomous' actually work in a contested link environment is invisible in their public language.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Same-day delivery to remote, high-risk field operations are a reality.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No mention anywhere of ATO/RMF, CMMC/NIST 800-171, ITAR/export control, or airworthiness certification despite scaling to a $37M USAF production contract for a hybrid-fuel VTOL aircraft.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A 'rapidly scale' production contract implies a compressed timeline; compliance and airworthiness certification gates are exactly the kind of unaddressed requirement that eats the funded months remaining on a transition contract before the aircraft is ever fielded at volume.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company culture and messaging is engineering/manufacturing-forward ('exemplary build quality', flight-test iteration count) rather than compliance-forward; compliance risk is invisible until a contracting officer forces it.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: With nearly 200 test flights already performed and its impressive flight envelope, it will be ready to handle the harshest and most demanding of missions in 2026.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Heavy-fuel (JP-5/Jet A-1) VTOL aircraft flown to 'challenging locations' with no mention of who refuels, maintains, or trains ground crew to sustain the fleet at a remote or forward site.
blind_spots.operator_reality: An autonomous aircraft is only as reliable as its ground logistics chain; the E-5 equivalent maintainer at an austere site needs spares, fuel logistics, and training that is never named — the company's own value prop ('critical parts can arrive at challenging locations on time, on repeat') ironically depends on a sustainment discipline it never describes for its own aircraft.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Product narrative centers on the airframe's performance envelope, not the deployed sustainment ecosystem that keeps a fielded fleet flying.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Critical parts can arrive at challenging locations on time, on repeat.

opener_hook: Skyways' $37M AFWERX contract funds scaling V3 into fielded ops in 2026. What's the C2/telemetry plan when the link goes denied?
what_they_do: Designs and flies long-range hybrid-VTOL autonomous cargo drones for military resupply and oil & gas logistics, now scaling V3 production under a $37M USAF AFWERX contract.
